impact: Per Pillar: a low-privilege triage agent could trigger a maintainer-only Gemini workflow, and a separate issue exposed a bot access token and a cloud service-account credential to the CI runner. Proof-of-concept; Google fixed it; no confirmed malicious exploitation.
mitigations: Pillar recommends giving agents narrowly scoped auditable identities, minimum tools and tokens, treating any agent that reads untrusted input as attacker-controlled, and preventing cross-privilege agent triggering without controls injected content cannot forge. Google removed the affected workflows, hardened the repository and added an internal review step.
name: Pillar: low-privilege triage agent could trigger privileged Gemini workflows on Google's ADK repository

sources.title: I'll Just Call You: Agent-to-Agent Privilege Boundary Failures in CI/CD on Google's ADK Repository

summary: Pillar Security disclosed on 2026-08-03, through Google's Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program, that a low-privilege public-facing triage agent in the CI/CD of Google's Agent Development Kit repository (google/adk-python) could be manipulated into triggering a higher-privilege maintainer-only Gemini workflow. A second issue let an externally authored issue drive a privileged agent workflow that exposed a bot access token and a cloud service-account credential to the CI runner. Pillar reported the issues on 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-05; the affected workflows were removed by 2026-07-02 and Google confirmed a fix on 2026-07-21. The work was proof-of-concept in a controlled project with no confirmed malicious exploitation, though Pillar observed other actors probing the same surface and shared logs with Google.
